candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Orationes contra Arianos III.54
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos (Four Discourses Against the Arians, I-IV), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.54 (c. 350 AD)

'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' (LXX 21:2 — ho theos ho theos mou, prosches moi, hina ti enkatelipes me) — Athanasius marks the CRY-OF-DERELICTION as voiced-by-the-assumed-flesh, NOT by the divine-Word as such. The divine-Word cannot be forsaken by the Father (Jn 16:32 — kai ouk eimi monos, hoti ho Patēr met' emou estin — 'and I am not alone, for the Father is with me'); the Word remains-eternally-with-the-Father even through the cross. The cry is voiced by the Word-IN-the-flesh, redeeming-from-within the human-experience of God-forsakenness. This anti-patripassian reading is CONSTITUTIVE for Tewahedo Holy-Friday Trisagion: 'Holy God who was crucified FOR US' — qua-flesh-suffered, qua-Word-impassible.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Athanasius of Alexandria, Orationes contra Arianos III.54. 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' (LXX 21:2 — ho theos ho theos mou, prosches moi, hina ti enkatelipes me) — Athanasius marks the CRY-OF-DERELICTION as voiced-by-the-assumed-flesh, NOT by the divine-Word as such. This anti-patripassian reading is CONSTITUTIVE for Tewahedo Holy-Friday Trisagion: 'Holy God who was crucified FOR US' — qua-flesh-suffered, qua-Word-impassible.
